proposals.evidence: Platts labels shikār Persian and includes hunting, prey and game; Zoller’s full footnote explicitly compares West Pahari śikār “game; meat”, supporting the regional semantic extension. The existing Hindi sikār donor proxy has a direct-source Hindi comparison (Bhattacharya) and is used here as a provisional Hindi/Urdu route. Both the donor proxy and local transmission remain provisional; the analysis does not skip directly to a remote Indo-Iranian root. Syllable-reduced and śakkar-like ambiguous responses are excluded.
